questions.question:
Choose the option that has an error in the sentence.

The more a culture expand, the less chance there is that it will become extinct.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The sentence contains a grammatical error in the phrase "**The more a culture expand**."
 
• The verb "**expand**" should be in its singular form "**expands**" to agree with the singular subject "**a culture**."
 
• In sentences that follow this comparative structure ("The more... the less"), subject-verb agreement must be maintained for grammatical correctness.
 
• Thus, the error lies in **Option 1**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The more a culture **expands**, the less chance there is that it will become extinct."*

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct usage of "less" and "fewer".

options.text: She has less books than I do.
There are fewer sugar in the jar.
We need fewer volunteers this time.
He has fewer money than his brother.

questions.solution:
The** correct answer** is **Option 3** i.e. **We need fewer volunteers this time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"fewer"** is used for **countable nouns** (things you can count individually, like books, people, or volunteers).** **
 
• The word **"less"** is used for **uncountable nouns** (things that are seen as a mass or bulk quantity and cannot be counted individually, like water, sugar, or air).
 
• In **Option 3**, **"volunteers"** is a countable noun, so **"fewer"** is the correct grammatical choice.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is:** Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Books" are countable. It should be: "She has **fewer** books than I do."
 
• **Option 2: **"Sugar" is uncountable. It should be: "There is **less** sugar in the jar."
 
• **Option 4: **While we count currency, the word **"money"** itself is treated as an uncountable mass noun. It should be: "He has **less** money than his brother." (Note: You would use "fewer" for specific units, like "fewer dollars").

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The officer said, "The library will be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month."

options.text: The officer said that the library would be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
The officer said that the library must be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
The officer said that the library has to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
The officer said that the library ought to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The sentence provided is in indirect speech, where the reporting verb "said" has been used.
 
• **Key Conversion:**
 
 
• The direct speech, "The library will be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month," is converted to indirect speech by changing "will" to "would" to maintain the sequence of tenses.
 
• The phrase "the library will be supplied" becomes "the library would be supplied" in indirect narration.
 
• The rest of the sentence remains the same as it does not require additional changes for accurate indirect narration.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• In indirect speech, quotation marks are removed.
 
• The sentence is restructured with the reporting verb followed by the indirect statement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** The officer said that the library would be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** The officer said that the library must be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
 
 
• Incorrect as "must" changes the modality and meaning of the sentence, implying an obligation rather than a statement of future supply.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The officer said that the library has to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
 
 
• Incorrect as "has to be supplied" uses present tense, which does not align with the past reporting verb "said."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The officer said that the library ought to be supplied with sufficient number of books within one month.
 
 
• Incorrect as "ought to be supplied" changes the tone of the statement, indicating a suggestion or moral obligation rather than a factual statement.
 
 
</ul

__
 
• To convert a sentence from passive voice to active voice, the subject of the passive sentence becomes the object in the active sentence, and the object of the passive sentence becomes the subject.
 
• The given sentence in the passive voice is: "The report is being reviewed by the manager."
 
• Here, "The report" is the subject in the passive sentence, and "the manager" is the agent performing the action.
 
• To convert it to active voice, make "the manager" the subject and "the report" the object.
 
• The verb form "is being reviewed" in the passive voice is changed to "is reviewing" in the active voice to maintain the present continuous tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The manager is reviewing the report."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2: **"The report is reviewing the manager." – Incorrect because it reverses the roles of the subject and object, leading to an illogical sentence.
 
• **Option 4: **"The manager had reviewed the report." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to past perfect instead of present continuous.

questions.question:
“Mental health has emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being”.

Rewrite the sentence as a negative sentence without changing its meaning.

options.text: Mental health has not failed to emerge as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health has not emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health doesn’t emerge as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health never emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: Mental health has not failed to emerge...***

 
 
• To change an affirmative sentence into a negative one without changing its meaning, we often use a **double negative** or an antonym.
 
• The phrase "has not failed to emerge" is logically equivalent to "has emerged." By using "not" + "failed," the sentence becomes grammatically negative while maintaining the original factual statement.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Mental health has not emerged...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect** because it directly contradicts the original passage. It changes the meaning from "it is a component" to "it is not a component."
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Mental health doesn’t emerge...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Similar to Option 2, it changes the meaning to a negative fact. Additionally, it changes the tense from Present Perfect ("has emerged") to Simple Present ("doesn't emerge").
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Mental health never emerged...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. It changes the meaning to suggest that the event never happened at all, which is the opposite of the author's intent.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transformation Rules**: When converting Affirmative to Negative without changing meaning: 

 
 
• Use **Not + Antonym**: (e.g., "He is a good boy" becomes "He is *not a bad* boy").
 
• Use **Double Negatives**: (e.g., "I remember you" becomes "I do *not forget* you").
 
 
 
• **Context**: In the passage, the author highlights mental health as a positive, emerging priority. Option 1 is the only one that upholds this perspective while satisfying the grammatical requirement for a negative word ("not").

Suresh is 22nd from the front.

Position from front = Total people - Position from back + 1

questions.question: Virashaiva movement begun in ______ in the mid-twelfth century.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Virashaiva movement**, also known as the **Lingayat movement**, originated in the state of **Karnataka** during the **mid-twelfth century**.
 
• This movement was spearheaded by **Basavanna**, a philosopher, poet, and statesman, who served as the Prime Minister of the Kalachuri Kingdom.
 
• The movement emphasized **monotheism** and rejected the caste system, idol worship, and ritualistic practices, advocating for social equality and spiritual devotion to Lord Shiva.
 
• Virashaivism or Lingayatism gained significant traction among the common people, especially the lower castes, due to its focus on **egalitarian principles**.
 
• The followers of this movement, called **Lingayats**, carry a small Shiva Linga encased in a pendant, symbolizing their devotion to Lord Shiva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Basavanna and His Teachings:**

 
 
• **Basavanna** was the founder of the Virashaiva movement. He is celebrated for his **Vachanas** (verses), which propagate a direct connection with God without the need for intermediaries like priests.
 
• He advocated for the formation of a **society based on equality**, rejecting the rigid caste-based hierarchy.
 
• Basavanna’s teachings laid the foundation for **social reform** in medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Philosophy of Virashaivism:**
 
 
• Virashaivism is monotheistic, focusing on the worship of **Lord Shiva**.
 
• It emphasizes **simple living**, ethical conduct, and devotion over ritualistic practices.
 
• The movement rejects the authority of the Vedas, caste discrimination, and idol worship.
 
 
 
• **Spread of the Movement:**
 
 
• Initially concentrated in Karnataka, the movement later spread to other parts of South India, including **Maharashtra** and **Telangana**.
 
• The Lingayat community became a significant socio-political force in southern India.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Virashaiva Movement:**
 
 
• The movement has had a lasting influence on the **socio-religious structure** of Karnataka and neighboring regions.
 
• Modern-day Lingayats continue to be a major community in Karnataka, influencing its culture, politics, and economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Movements of the Period:**

 
 
• The **Bhakti Movement**, which flourished during the same time, shared similarities with the Virashaiva movement, such as its rejection of caste and ritualism.
 
• Other prominent leaders of the Bhakti Movement included **Ramananda, Kabir, and Mirabai**, though their philosophies varied from that of the Lingayats.
 
 
 
• **Modern Recognition:**
 
 
• In recent years, there has been a movement to recognize the Lingayats as a separate religion, distinct from mainstream Hinduism.
 
• The Karnataka government, in **2018**, recommended the Lingayat community be granted **minority religion status**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To respect one's parents and teachers
To take part in village panchayat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To safeguard public property**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Fundamental Duties** are enshrined in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution, added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**. These duties are meant to promote a sense of responsibility and discipline among citizens. 
• The duty **“To safeguard public property”** is explicitly mentioned under the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution. It emphasizes citizens' role in protecting and conserving public infrastructure and national assets. 
• The Fundamental Duties were inspired by the **Soviet Constitution** and aim to inculcate civic and moral values in Indian citizens. 
• Examples of safeguarding public property include protecting historical monuments, public transportation, government buildings, and preventing vandalism or misuse. 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-enforceable by law but are crucial for the nation's collective welfare and ethical governance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Article 51A and Fundamental Duties:** 
• **Article 51A** lists **11 Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens. These were introduced through the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1976**. 
• Some of the Fundamental Duties include **respecting the Constitution**, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and safeguarding public property. 
• The **86th Amendment Act, 2002** added the duty for parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to children aged **6-14 years**. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the **USSR (Soviet Union)** and other socialist countries. 
• They were introduced during the tenure of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi** to counteract the growing indiscipline and foster a sense of responsibility among citizens. 
• **Legal Framework:** 
• Though Fundamental Duties are **non-justiciable**, laws can be enacted to enforce them indirectly. For instance, laws against vandalism protect public property. 
• Some Fundamental Duties have been linked to legal provisions such as the **Environmental Protection Act, 1986**, which aligns with the duty to protect the natural environment. 
• **Comparison with Fundamental Rights:** 
• While Fundamental Rights grant privileges and freedoms to citizens, Fundamental Duties emphasize moral obligations. 
• Rights and Duties are interconnected, as enjoying rights comes with the responsibility to perform duties for the welfare of society. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Fundamental Duties in Detail:** 
• There are a total of **11 Fundamental Duties**, which include respecting national symbols, promoting harmony, and protecting the environment. 
• The duty to safeguard public property ensures the integrity and functionality of assets vital to public welfare. 
• **Examples of Safeguarding Public Property:** 
• Participating in campaigns against vandalism. 
• Ensuring responsible use of public transport and facilities. 
• Encouraging awareness about the importance of conserving national heritage sites. 
• **Significance of Fundamental Duties:** 
• They act as a **moral compass** for citizens, promoting national unity and responsibility. 
• They complement Fundamental Rights by instilling a sense of accountability towards the nation.

• **'Raas Leela'** performances are a significant cultural and spiritual element of the festival of **Holi**, particularly in the regions of **Mathura** and **Vrindavan**.
 
• Holi celebrates the divine love of **Lord Krishna** and **Radha**. The festival is deeply rooted in the mythology and traditions of the Braj region, which includes Mathura, the birthplace of Krishna.
 
• During Holi, the **Raas Leela** (a dance-drama based on Krishna's playful and romantic interactions with the Gopis) is performed to reenact scenes from Krishna's life, especially his playful acts with Radha and the Gopis.
 
• The performances are accompanied by devotional music, folk songs, and colorful dances, symbolizing love, joy, and the victory of good over evil.
 
• Mathura and Vrindavan attract numerous tourists and devotees during Holi due to their vibrant celebrations, which include not only Raas Leela but also events like **Phoolon Ki Holi** (Holi with flowers) and **Lathmar Holi** (a playful tradition where women playfully hit men with sticks).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Holi:**

 
 
• **Holi** is an ancient Hindu festival celebrated in the month of **Phalguna** (February-March) as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• It is also known as the "Festival of Colors" and signifies the arrival of spring, the end of winter, and the blossoming of love.
 
• Holi is associated with several legends, including the story of **Prahlad** and **Holika**, symbolizing the victory of good over evil.
 
• Major events of Holi include the burning of the effigy of Holika (Holika Dahan) and the play with colors on the following day.
 
 
 
• **Raas Leela:**
 
 
• Raas Leela is a traditional **Indian folk dance** that originated in the Braj region, where Lord Krishna spent his childhood.
 
• It is a dramatization of the divine love story of Lord Krishna and Radha, depicting the playful and romantic aspects of their relationship.
 
• The dance is performed in a circular formation, symbolizing the eternal bond between the divine and the human soul.
 
• Raas Leela is often performed during festivals such as Holi and Janmashtami in temples and cultural programs.
 
 
 
• **Other Festivals Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Diwali:** Known as the Festival of Lights, Diwali celebrates the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. It is not associated with Raas Leela performances.
 
• **Chhath Puja:** This festival is dedicated to the worship of the Sun God and is celebrated primarily in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Nepal. It does not involve Raas Leela.
 
• **Raksha Bandhan:** A festival celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters. It has no connection to Raas Leela.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Phoolon Ki Holi:** In Vrindavan, Holi is celebrated with flowers instead of colors in the famous Banke Bihari Temple. It attracts devotees from across the globe.
 
• **Lathmar Holi:** Celebrated in Barsana and Nandgaon, this unique Holi tradition involves women playfully hitting men with sticks while men try to shield themselves.

questions.question: The rock-cut ratha temples at Mahabalipuram were built by the ______.
questions.solution:

__

• The rock-cut ratha temples at **Mahabalipuram**, also known as the **Pancha Rathas**, were constructed during the reign of the **Pallava dynasty** in the 7th century CE.

• The Pallava king **Narasimhavarman I**, also called **Mamalla**, is credited with initiating the construction of these iconic monuments.

• The temples are carved out of single rock formations (monolithic) and represent early forms of **Dravidian architecture**.

• The Pancha Rathas are named after the **five Pandava brothers** from the Mahabharata—Draupadi Ratha, Arjuna Ratha, Bhima Ratha, Dharmaraja Ratha, and Nakula-Sahadeva Ratha.

• The structures are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and are known for their intricate carvings and unique architectural style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• The Pallavas ruled parts of southern India from the 3rd to the 9th century CE, with their capital at **Kanchipuram**.

• They were renowned for their contributions to **art, architecture, and religion**, laying the foundations for later Dravidian temple architecture.

• Other famous architectural works of the Pallavas include the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram and the Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram.

• **Rock-Cut Architecture:**

• Rock-cut architecture involves the carving of structures directly into natural rock formations, often using a single stone.

• Examples include the Ajanta and Ellora caves in Maharashtra and the Mahabalipuram temples in Tamil Nadu.

• **Dravidian Architecture:**

• Dravidian architecture is characterized by pyramid-shaped towers (vimanas) and intricate carvings.

• It became prominent in South India during the Pallava, Chola, and Vijayanagara periods.

• **UNESCO Heritage Sites:**

• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram was designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in 1984.

• These monuments are celebrated for their historical significance and architectural brilliance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Cholas:**

• The Cholas ruled South India from the 9th to 13th century CE and were known for their grand temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur.

• **Cheras:**

• The Cheras were a prominent dynasty in ancient Kerala, known for trade and maritime activities rather than monumental architecture.

• **Mauryas:**

• The Maurya Empire (321–185 BCE) was known for its contributions to Indian art and architecture, such as the rock edicts of Ashoka, but they were not associated with South Indian architecture.

questions.question: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with which of the following treaty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Treaty of Salbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **First Anglo-Maratha War** (1775-1782) ended with the signing of the **Treaty of Salbai** in **1782** between the British East India Company and the Marathas.
 
• The treaty was negotiated by **Colonel Upton** on behalf of the British and was signed between the **Governor-General Warren Hastings** and the Maratha leader **Madhavrao II**.
 
• The treaty ensured a period of **peace between the British and the Marathas** for the next 20 years. It marked the end of hostilities between the two powers.
 
• Under the terms of the treaty, the Marathas retained control over most of their territories, including **Sindhia's territories in North India**, while the British gained control over **Salsette** and adjacent islands near Bombay.
 
• The treaty also recognized the **Shah Alam II**, a Mughal emperor, under Maratha protection, thereby cementing their influence in Northern India.
 
• This treaty is considered a significant event in Indian history as it showcased the **political diplomacy** and balance of power between the British and the Marathas during the late 18th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Anglo-Maratha War:**

 
 
• The war was primarily triggered by the **succession conflict** following the death of Maratha ruler Madhavrao I in 1772.
 
• The British supported **Raghunath Rao** (Raghoba), who sought to become the Peshwa, against the legitimate heir **Madhav Rao II** (Narayanrao's son).
 
• It lasted from **1775 to 1782** and involved a series of battles fought in various regions of India, including Maharashtra and Gujarat.
 
• The war ended inconclusively, leading to the Treaty of Salbai, which aimed to restore peace and resolve territorial disputes.
 
 
 
• **Treaty of Surat:**
 
 
• Signed in **1775**, it was an agreement between **Raghunath Rao** and the British East India Company.
 
• Under this treaty, Raghunath Rao promised the British control over **Salsette** and Bassein in exchange for their military support.
 
• This treaty led to the outbreak of the First Anglo-Maratha War, as other Maratha factions opposed British interference.
 
 
 
• **Treaty of Bassein (1802):**
 
 
• Signed between the British and the Maratha leader **Baji Rao II**, this treaty marked the beginning of British dominance over the Maratha Empire.
 
• It was a later treaty, not related to the First Anglo-Maratha War, but played a crucial role in the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-1805).
 
• Under this treaty, the Marathas accepted British protection and control over their foreign affairs.
 
 
 
• **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792):**
 
 
• This treaty was signed between the British, the Nizam of Hyderabad, and Tipu Sultan after the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
 
• It resulted in Tipu Sultan losing significant territories to the British and their allies.
 
• This treaty is unrelated to the First Anglo-Maratha War but is an important event in the history of British expansion in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Treaty of Salbai:**

 
 
• Ensured a stable political environment and prevented further British-Maratha wars for the next two decades.
 
• Strengthened Maratha influence in Northern India while allowing the British to expand their hold in Western India.
 
• Reflected the use of **diplomacy** rather than prolonged warfare to resolve conflicts.
 
 
 
• **Impact on British Expansion:**
 
 
• The treaty allowed the British to consolidate their position in Bombay and nearby regions.
 
• It marked the beginning of a strategic partnership between the British and certain Indian factions, a pattern seen in later conflicts.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution is related with the Special address by the Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 176**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 176** of the **Indian Constitution** mandates the **Governor** to address the first session of the State Legislature after a general election and the first session of each year.
 
• This is referred to as the **"Special Address"**, where the Governor outlines the policies and programs of the state government for the upcoming year.
 
• The address is delivered to a joint session of both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council (if applicable).
 
• The content of the Governor's address is prepared by the state government, and it acts as a policy statement, providing a blueprint for legislative and administrative priorities.
 
• The discussion on the Governor's address in the legislature allows members to deliberate on the policies and raise concerns or suggestions. **Hence, Article 176 is related to the Special Address by the Governor.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 175:**

 
 
• It empowers the **Governor** to address the Legislative Assembly or both Houses of the Legislature (if it is a bicameral legislature).
 
• The Governor can send messages to the legislature with respect to a bill or any other matter and require the legislature to consider it.
 
 
 
• **Article 177:**
 
 
• This article allows the **Advocate General of the State** and Ministers to participate in the proceedings of the State Legislature.
 
• However, they do not have the right to vote unless they are members of the legislature themselves.
 
 
 
• **Article 178:**
 
 
• It deals with the positions of the **Speaker** and **Deputy Speaker** of the Legislative Assembly in each state.
 
• The Speaker presides over the sessions of the Legislative Assembly, maintaining order and ensuring the smooth conduct of business.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The Governor is the **constitutional head** of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• The Governor's address in the legislature is a key constitutional requirement and sets the tone for legislative and executive priorities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Governor's Special Address** is an integral part of the parliamentary system and allows the government to communicate its vision and objectives to the legislature.
 
• The discussion on the Governor's address is an opportunity for the opposition to scrutinize the government's policies and actions.
 
• This address is similar to the **President's Address** to the Parliament at the commencement of the first session after each general election and the first session of each year under **Article 87** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• In case of a bicameral legislature, the address is delivered to a joint sitting of both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms does NOT use parasitic nutritive strategy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yeast**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Parasitic nutrition** is a mode of nutrition in which an organism (parasite) derives its food from another living organism (host), often harming the host in the process. 
• Organisms like **ticks**, **lice**, and **tapeworms** are classic examples of parasites as they depend on a host for their survival and nutrients. They often harm or weaken the host. 
• **Yeast**, on the other hand, does not exhibit parasitic nutrition. It follows a **saprophytic mode of nutrition**, obtaining nutrients from dead or decaying organic matter. 
• Yeast is a **unicellular fungus** that plays a crucial role in fermentation processes, such as the production of alcohol and bread-making. 
• Unlike parasites, yeast does not rely on living hosts for nutrition, making it fundamentally different from organisms like ticks, lice, and tapeworms. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Ticks:** 
• Ticks are ectoparasites that feed on the blood of mammals, birds, and sometimes reptiles and amphibians. 
• They can transmit diseases such as **Lyme disease** and **Rocky Mountain spotted fever**. 
• Ticks attach themselves to the host's skin and derive nutrients by sucking blood. 
• **Lice:** 
• Lice are small, wingless insects that live as parasites on the skin of mammals and birds. 
• They feed on the blood of their host and cause itching and irritation. 
• Examples include head lice, body lice, and pubic lice. 
• **Tapeworm:** 
• Tapeworms are intestinal parasites that live in the digestive tract of vertebrates, including humans. 
• They absorb nutrients directly from the host's digested food through their body surface. 
• Humans can become infected by consuming undercooked or contaminated meat containing tapeworm larvae. 
• **Yeast:** 
• Yeast is a type of fungus that reproduces asexually by budding. 
• It is used in various industrial processes such as **fermentation** to produce alcohol and carbon dioxide. 
• Yeast does not harm a living host and instead grows on non-living organic material. 
• An example of yeast is **Saccharomyces cerevisiae**, commonly used in baking and brewing. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Parasitic vs. Saprophytic Nutrition:** 
• **Parasites** depend on living hosts for food and often harm the host. 
• **Saprophytes**, like yeast, obtain nutrients from dead or decaying organic matter. 
• Parasites include organisms like ticks, lice, tapeworms, and certain bacteria. Examples of saprophytes include fungi like yeast and mushrooms. 
• **Role of Yeast in Industry:** 
• Yeast is extensively used in **fermentation processes** for producing beer, wine, and bread. 
• It is also used in the biotechnology sector for producing **enzymes** and **bioethanol**. 
• **Diseases Caused by Parasites:** 
• Parasites like ticks and lice can cause diseases such as **anemia**, **skin irritation**, and **vector-borne illnesses**. 
• Tapeworm infections can lead to symptoms like abdominal pain, malnutrition, and weight loss. </ul
